newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Transneft, AIOC, SOCAR sign pipeline agreement.
newsitem.headline: Transneft, AIOC, SOCAR sign pipeline agreement.

text.p: A multinational Caspian Sea oil consortium and Russian oil pipeline monopoly AO Transneft have signed agreements to send oil to the Novorossiisk Black Sea port in a Transneft pipeline, a company official said on Friday.
The agreement was signed by the Azerbaijan International Operating Co (AIOC), Transneft and Azeri state oil company SOCAR on March 27, the official said.
Oil will begin flowing in October, by which time a 150-kilometer section of the pipeline in the war-torn Chechnya would be repaired, he said.
The agreement covers the so-called northern route for Caspian oil. A southern route through the former Soviet republic of Georgia is also planned.
The Transneft official said the 1997 oil flow from the Azeri, Chirag and Gunashli fields in the Caspian Sea would amount to 20,000 tonnes .
AIOC is a 13-member international consortium led by an alliance of British Petroleum and Norway's Statoil. It includes Amoco Corp and Exxon.
The fields contain four billion barrels of crude reserves, allowing output to reach 700,000 bpd in the first half of the next decade, AIOC President Terence Adams has estimated.
